channel.title: IT Threat Intel - IT Cybersecurity
channel.description: Curated IT / enterprise cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Attackers went global on VMware vCenter within days of the patch — 361 victim IPs across 47 countries, with reverse_ssh left behind on the virtualization control plane
item.description: A critical directory-traversal flaw in the VMware vCenter Server syslog service, CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8), gives an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution, and it is now being exploited at scale. Broadcom shipped fixes on 29 July 2026; DFIR firm QUIRSO recorded first contact with attacker-controlled infrastructure on 3 August, just five days later, and had counted 361 distinct victim IP addresses across 47 countries by 7 August, concentrated heavily in Germany, the United States, Turkey, Iran and France. The observed intrusion chain runs from path-traversal activity consistent with the flaw, to a malicious cron job for persistence, to deployment of the open-source reverse_ssh framework to hold a covert command-and-control channel. Researchers assess with moderate confidence that a suspected China-nexus operator is behind the activity and is dropping a Babuk-derived ransomware variant, which some believe functions as a smokescreen for deeper, quieter intrusion rather than as the actual goal — that attribution and motive are assessed, not confirmed. vCenter is the management plane for the virtualization estate: whoever controls it can typically reach every guest VM, every datastore and, in most environments, the backup infrastructure too, which is exactly why it is such a high-value target. The flaw is not yet listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of this edition despite the scale of observed exploitation. Fixed builds are vCenter 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100, and the patched 8.0 U3 and U2 lines. Any organisation running an internet- or broadly-network-reachable vCenter instance that was not patched by early August should assume compromise is possible and hunt accordingly, not merely patch and move on. - The Hacker News / BleepingComputer (QUIRSO research) - Patched 29 Jul 2026; exploitation observed from 3 Aug; reported 13 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] Cl0p’s PTC Windchill extortion campaign lists dozens of victims — only Philips has confirmed a breach so far
item.description: An affiliate exploiting CVE-2026-12569, an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in PTC Windchill (CVSS 9.3), chained it with a pre-authentication information-disclosure bug in FlexPLM and a Windchill login-servlet flaw to reach remote code execution and drop JSP web shells, according to ReliaQuest, with activity ramping from 20 July. PTC began patching 17 June and CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog in late June, but exploitation started within a day of the fix shipping. Cl0p has listed roughly 43–50 organisations as victims on its leak site, including Shell (with an alleged 89GB of data), GE, Fiserv and Philips. Philips has confirmed it suffered a breach; Shell and GE say they are still investigating and have not confirmed the claims; the remainder of the list is Cl0p’s claim alone and unverified. The material at stake is engineering-grade product lifecycle data — drawings, test reports, facility photos and project plans — not typical customer PII, which raises the stakes for manufacturers and their supply chains specifically. - BleepingComputer (ReliaQuest research) - Patched 17 Jun 2026; exploitation from 20 Jul; reported 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] ShinyHunters dumps a 280GB RingCentral archive covering roughly 1.6 million accounts after a social-engineering breach
item.description: RingCentral has confirmed a breach that began with a social-engineering campaign against its staff or systems. After the company declined to pay, extortion group ShinyHunters published a roughly 280GB archive it says covers about 1.6 million accounts, including names, email addresses, phone numbers and mailing addresses. There is no indication that call content, recordings or payment-card data were included, but the exposed contact information is enough to fuel targeted phishing and vishing against both RingCentral customers and their end users. Given RingCentral’s footprint in enterprise unified communications, organisations that rely on it should expect a wave of impersonation attempts referencing real account details. - SecurityWeek - Breach reported 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] A ransomware crew hijacked a hospital system’s Facebook page mid-incident to publicize its extortion demands
item.description: AnMed Health System, a four-hospital operator in Georgia and South Carolina, was hit by a cyberattack on 26 July that disabled IT systems and left ten facilities closed to appointments for over a week. On 11 August, a group calling itself “The Gentlemen” took over AnMed’s Facebook page to post ransom demands and claim it holds 6TB of health data. AnMed has not verified the group’s claims about the volume or content of stolen data. The public hijacking of an official social-media account is itself a notable tactic — it pressures the victim publicly and complicates incident-response communications while core clinical IT systems are still being restored. - The Record - Facebook hijack reported 11 Aug 2026; original attack 26 Jul 2026

item.title: [High] A worm in the npm package keyv used stolen credentials to poison hundreds of packages within about 30 minutes
item.description: A supply-chain worm compromised the widely-used npm package keyv using stolen publishing credentials, then used that foothold to automatically poison hundreds of further packages in roughly half an hour, according to The Hacker News. The malicious versions harvested developer credentials, CI/CD tokens and cloud API keys from build environments, and in some cases planted hooks in editor or task-runner configuration that could trigger the payload later. The speed of propagation is the headline risk: automated dependency-poisoning worms can outrun manual detection and typical patch-review cycles, and any organisation that pulled affected package versions during the window should assume its build pipeline credentials may be compromised. - The Hacker News - Reported 12 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] North Carolina Ports confirms an outside actor breached IT systems at all three facilities, forcing manual processing
item.description: North Carolina Ports confirmed that an outside actor breached its IT systems on 5 August, affecting the Wilmington and Morehead City seaports as well as the Charlotte inland terminal; the incident was publicly reported the next day. A spokesperson confirmed the intrusion and said cargo processing switched to manual procedures, but declined to say whether ransomware was involved. Normal operating schedules resumed by 6–7 August, though some processing reportedly remained manual afterward. The operator describes the breach as contained to IT systems, but has not explicitly ruled out any touch on operational technology used for crane or terminal operations — that distinction has not been confirmed either way, and should not be assumed in either direction. - The Record - Intrusion 5 Aug 2026; reported 6 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] CISA and the FBI detail Gunra, a Conti-derived ransomware operation hitting healthcare, government and critical infrastructure
item.description: A joint CISA/FBI #StopRansomware advisory, AA26-222A, published 10 August, profiles Gunra, a double-extortion ransomware-as-a-service operation whose code is derived from the leaked Conti source. The advisory says Gunra affiliates gain initial access through internet-facing VPN gateways and firewalls, citing exploitation of known Fortinet flaws CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 among the entry vectors, and that the group has targeted healthcare, government and other critical-infrastructure sectors with double extortion — encrypting data while also stealing it for leverage. Both cited Fortinet CVEs already have patches and are established KEV entries; the advisory is a reminder that unpatched, internet-exposed network edge devices remain the most common door for ransomware crews long after fixes exist, not a report of a new vulnerability. - CISA / FBI advisory AA26-222A - Published 10 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] Mustang Panda adds a signed kernel-mode rootkit to its CoolClient backdoor, hiding behind an expired 2013 certificate
item.description: Chinese state-linked espionage group Mustang Panda has added a signed Windows kernel-mode rootkit to its CoolClient backdoor, according to The Hacker News, using a code-signing certificate from 2013 that has since expired but which Windows will still load under older driver-signing rules. The rootkit hides malicious processes and network activity from standard monitoring tools, making the backdoor harder to detect once installed. The activity has been observed against government targets in Myanmar, Mongolia, Pakistan and Russia. The technique — abusing legacy signed drivers to run kernel-mode code — is not new, but its continued effectiveness is a reminder that driver-signing policy and allow-lists deserve periodic review rather than a one-time setup. - The Hacker News - Reported 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [Medium] A claimed 3.6-million-record Azure/Entra data-theft campaign is disputed by several of the named companies
item.description: An actor using the handle “TheHatman” claims to have stolen roughly 3.6 million employee-directory records from Microsoft Azure/Entra tenants at companies including McDonald’s, TCS, Vodafone (about 425,000 records), HCL and IHG, via password-spray and MFA-fatigue attacks. The claim is disputed: several of the named companies say they have found no evidence of the described breach, and researchers who reviewed samples of the data suggest it may originate from older infostealer logs rather than a fresh Entra compromise. Treat the specific attribution and scale as unconfirmed. What is not in dispute is that password spray and MFA fatigue remain effective against tenants without phishing-resistant authentication, regardless of whether this particular claim holds up. - SecurityWeek - Claim reported 12 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] Researchers trace most of a 2,500-organisation secrets leak to a March compromise of the Trivy scanner, not the LiteLLM packages that drew initial attention
item.description: Follow-up analysis has revised the picture of a supply-chain incident that initially centred on poisoned LiteLLM packages: SecurityWeek reports that most of the roughly 2,500 organisations whose secrets leaked were actually exposed through a March compromise of Aqua Security’s Trivy vulnerability scanner and its Docker images, with the later LiteLLM poisoning a separate, smaller contributor. The correction matters operationally — teams that checked only their LiteLLM exposure and moved on may have missed a Trivy-based leak path in CI/CD pipelines that ran the affected scanner images months earlier. - SecurityWeek - Reported 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] Metabase’s CVSS-10 SQL injection was exploited as a zero-day before a patch existed — Framework and Trezor’s fulfilment partner both confirm breaches
item.description: CVE-2026-72898, an unauthenticated SQL injection in Metabase’s /reset_password endpoint that grants admin access, carries the maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and was added to CISA’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 August with a federal remediation deadline of 14 August. It affects open-source Metabase 0.58.0 through 0.63.x before 0.63.5, and Enterprise 1.58.0 through 1.63.x before 1.63.5. Attackers exploited it before a patch was available. Two confirmed victims have disclosed breaches so far: laptop maker Framework, whose 3 August notice covers names, emails, addresses, phone numbers and billing information for its full customer base; and ShipMonk, the fulfilment partner for hardware-wallet maker Trezor, affecting roughly 13,689 Trezor customers — Trezor has said no seed phrases or private keys were exposed. - BleepingComputer / TechCrunch - KEV added 11 Aug 2026; Framework and Trezor disclosures 3–8 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] A max-severity SAP Commerce Cloud flaw drew exploitation attempts within three days of its patch, with 4,200+ instances exposed
item.description: CVE-2026-58231, an improper-authorization flaw in SAP Commerce Cloud’s Data Hub Adapter that allows arbitrary code execution, carries a CVSS score of 10.0. SAP patched it on 11 August, and exploitation attempts hit security researchers’ honeypots within three days, with a public proof-of-concept following shortly after. Shadowserver counted more than 4,200 internet-exposed SAP Commerce Cloud instances at the time of reporting. As a widely-deployed e-commerce and digital-commerce platform, unpatched exposed instances are a direct path to customer and transaction data as well as a foothold into connected backend SAP environments. - BleepingComputer - Patched 11 Aug 2026; exploitation attempts reported 15 Aug 2026

item.title: [Critical] An authentication-bypass flaw in macOS Screen Sharing is being scanned for and used to plant cryptominers — roughly 40,000 Macs remain exposed
item.description: CVE-2026-65400, an authentication-bypass flaw in macOS Screen Sharing, carries a CVSS score of 9.8. Attackers are scanning the internet for Macs with the Screen Sharing port (5900) exposed, using the bypass to gain root access and install Monero cryptomining malware. The Netherlands’ NCSC-NL estimates roughly 40,000 Macs remain reachable via the service despite Apple’s fix. Apple patched the flaw on 6 August in macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, Sequoia 15.7.9 and Sonoma 14.8.9. Enterprises that manage fleets of Macs, particularly ones used as remote-access jump points or shared lab machines, should not assume this is a consumer-only issue. - SecurityWeek (NCSC-NL) - Patched 6 Aug 2026; exposure estimate reported 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] Microsoft’s August Patch Tuesday fixes 398 CVEs, including one exploited local elevation-of-privilege zero-day tied to a North Korean backdoor campaign
item.description: Microsoft’s August 2026 Patch Tuesday addressed 398 CVEs. Exactly one was under active exploitation at release: CVE-2026-68820, a use-after-free vulnerability in the Windows Ancillary Function Driver for WinSock (afd.sys), rated CVSS 7.0. It is a local elevation-of-privilege flaw — an attacker needs existing code execution on the machine to use it to gain higher privileges, not an unauthenticated remote entry point. Check Point ties exploitation of this flaw to North Korea’s Lazarus Group, used in its “Operation Dream Job” campaign: trojanised PDF viewers and DLL side-loading deliver a new backdoor Check Point calls Troy, targeting defence and aerospace organisations in France, Germany, Brazil and India. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 11 August. Because this is a local-privilege-escalation bug, its danger is realized after an attacker has already landed via phishing or another initial-access method — which is exactly the Lazarus delivery chain observed here. - The Hacker News (Check Point research) / ZDI - Patch Tuesday and KEV listing 11 Aug 2026

item.title: [High] GeoServer patches an unauthenticated SQL injection that saw internet-wide scanning within hours of disclosure — no CVE has been assigned
item.description: GeoServer shipped fixes in versions 3.0.1, 2.28.5 and 2.27.6 on 14 August for an unauthenticated SQL injection in the jsonArrayContains filter used against PostGIS layers, tracked under advisory id GHSA-mqjf-5f49-2fjh. No CVE number has been assigned to the flaw as of this edition, and the GeoServer project itself rates the issue “High” severity without publishing a CVSS score — figures circulating elsewhere citing a 9.8 or similar score are not sourced to the project. Exploitation attempts began within hours of the 12 August disclosure, ahead of the 14 August patch. GeoServer is common in government GIS, agricultural mapping, telecom network-planning and transit-authority systems, so its user base skews toward public-sector and infrastructure-adjacent organisations that may not treat a mapping server as a top patching priority. - GeoServer project advisory - Disclosed 12 Aug 2026; patched 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] CISA publishes two free K-12 cybersecurity guides as ransomware keeps hitting schools
item.description: CISA released two free guidance documents for K-12 school districts on 14 August, covering credential protection, device security, backup testing, incident-response planning and adoption of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework. The agency cites 34 ransomware attacks against K-12 and higher-education institutions in the first half of 2026 and points to the March breach at Alamo Heights ISD, which affected 26,629 people, as an example of the stakes. The guidance is voluntary and non-regulatory, aimed at districts that often lack dedicated security staff or budget. - K-12 Dive - Published 14 Aug 2026

item.title: [Info] The judge overseeing Change Healthcare breach litigation imposes strict new rules on how the exposed dataset can be used
item.description: The federal judge overseeing multidistrict litigation stemming from the 2024 Change Healthcare ransomware breach has imposed new, stricter rules governing how the enormous dataset exposed in that incident may be handled and used by parties to the litigation going forward. The order tightens data-handling and security requirements around one of the largest healthcare data exposures on record, reflecting continued judicial and regulatory attention to how breached personal health information is managed even years after the original incident. It is a reminder that the operational and legal tail of a major breach extends well past the initial incident-response window. - Court filing coverage - Reported 12 Aug 2026
